options_evaluated: 100% Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) Polypropylene (PP) with 20% glass fiber reinforcement
decisions.trade_off: Balancing the lower carbon footprint of recycled polymers against the mechanical durability, impact resistance, and long-term fatigue life required for a power tool housing.
decisions.recommendation: 100% Post-Consumer Recycled (PCR) Polypropylene (PP) with 20% glass fiber reinforcement
decisions.rationale: PCR PP with glass fiber significantly reduces Scope 3 embodied carbon compared to virgin engineering plastics. The glass fiber reinforcement provides the necessary structural rigidity and drop-impact resistance to ensure a long product lifespan, preventing premature disposal.
decisions.design_action: Verify the supply chain consistency and mechanical property tolerances of PCR PP suppliers, and check compatibility with standard injection molding shrinkage rates.

options_evaluated: Removable machine screws into recycled steel threaded inserts
decisions.trade_off: Permanent joining minimizes assembly parts and weight but prevents non-destructive disassembly, whereas threaded inserts facilitate easy repair and recycling but increase part count and manufacturing energy.
decisions.recommendation: Removable machine screws into recycled steel threaded inserts
decisions.rationale: This approach prioritizes end-of-life disassembly and repairability. Users or technicians can easily open the housing to replace worn gears or the battery without damaging the casing, extending the product's useful life and enabling clean material separation during recycling.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the availability of standardized fastener sizes and check the feasibility of minimizing the number of unique screw heads to simplify disassembly tools.

options_evaluated: Brushed DC motor with ferrite magnets
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with Neodymium (NdFeB) rare-earth magnets
Brushless DC motor with iron-nitride magnets (rare-earth-free)
decisions.trade_off: BLDC motors offer much higher energy efficiency and operational lifespan but rely on rare-earth magnets which have severe environmental extraction impacts.
decisions.recommendation: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with Neodymium (NdFeB) rare-earth magnets
decisions.rationale: The high efficiency of the BLDC motor reduces energy consumption during use, and the absence of brushes dramatically extends the motor's lifespan (often the primary failure point in brushed tools). The environmental impact of the rare-earth magnets is offset by the extended product life, provided the magnets can be recovered at end-of-life.
decisions.design_action: Verify the feasibility of a modular motor mount design that allows easy extraction of the rotor and magnet assembly during end-of-life recycling.

options_evaluated: Active cooling via an integrated fan on the motor shaft
Passive cooling via optimized housing vents and internal air paths
Passive cooling using a phase-change material (PCM) heat sink
decisions.trade_off: Active cooling increases power density but introduces noise, dust ingress (reducing lifespan), and parasitic energy loss, whereas passive cooling is highly reliable but requires larger surface areas or specialized materials.
decisions.recommendation: Passive cooling via optimized housing vents and internal air paths
decisions.rationale: Eliminating an active fan reduces mechanical complexity, prevents internal dust accumulation (which degrades electronics and gears in dusty DIY environments), and avoids parasitic energy draw, thereby extending battery life and overall product reliability.
decisions.design_action: Investigate the thermal limits of the selected BLDC motor and driver under continuous stall conditions to check if passive dissipation is sufficient.

options_evaluated: Modular cartridge system (separate battery, motor/gearbox, and trigger/electronics modules)
Semi-modular layout with soldered wire connections
decisions.trade_off: A modular cartridge system increases initial material use and volume but allows rapid, toolless, or simple tool-based replacement of individual failed components.
decisions.recommendation: Modular cartridge system (separate battery, motor/gearbox, and trigger/electronics modules)
decisions.rationale: Power tools often fail due to a single component, such as a worn switch or degraded battery cell. A modular architecture allows the user to replace only the failed module, preventing the entire tool from becoming electronic waste and supporting circular economy principles.
decisions.design_action: Check the availability of standardized, slide-in blind-mate connectors to eliminate internal wiring harnesses and simplify module swap-out.

decisions.trade_off: Integrated batteries allow a smaller, lighter tool but render the tool useless once the battery degrades, whereas interchangeable packs increase weight and volume but dramatically extend product life.
decisions.rationale: Removable battery packs prevent the tool from being discarded when the battery degrades (the most common failure mode in cordless tools). By incorporating USB-C charging directly on the battery or tool, it eliminates the need for proprietary charging bricks, reducing global e-waste.
decisions.design_action: Investigate industry-standard battery pack interfaces or open-standard battery alliances to check compatibility with existing charging platforms.
